clue.text: Wildly enthusiastic fiddle accompanying a line in song

parts.note: mad about something means wildly enthusiastic about it
to fiddle or rig a result is to manipulate it dishonestly

explanation.surface: Someone frantically plays the fiddle as backing to a single line of a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' looks like the violin, but here it is the verb meaning to cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: A madrigal is a part-song for several unaccompanied voices, popular in Renaissance England.

clue.text: Take nothing from marketplace in city out East

indicators.note: take, paired with from, tells us to remove one piece from another
from names the word that loses the letter in this removal

parts.note: the agora was the public marketplace of an ancient Greek city
O, the zero shape, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A trader is told to remove nothing from a bazaar in an Eastern city.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the O from AGORA to leave the city in India home to the Taj Mahal.
explanation.definitionFit: Agra is a city in northern India, the far East from a British viewpoint.

clue.text: Ensuing when most of the fruit is put in to soak

indicators.note: put in tells us one piece goes inside another, here the shortened fruit inside the soaking word

parts.note: to ret is to soak flax or hemp to soften it

indicators.note: most of means the final letter of the fruit word is dropped

parts.note: a sultana is a dried grape

explanation.surface: What follows when dried fruit is put in water to soak before baking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' looks like it describes the fruit being added to a bowl; to ret is a technical word for steeping flax or hemp.
explanation.definitionFit: A resultant effect is one that follows on as a consequence, synonymous with ensuing.

clue.text: Outbuilding in, say, a rough slate put up

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the pieces are read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: EG, for example, is signalled by say
rag is a coarse, rough roofing slate or stone

explanation.surface: A shed is made of a coarse slate raised into place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns the whole run round, as this is a down clue; rag is a builders' term for a coarse roofing slate.
explanation.definitionFit: A garage is a separate building for keeping a car, a typical outbuilding beside a house.

clue.text: Take the opposite view and turn a blind eye

definitions.meaning: literally, gaze in the other direction

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both facing away physically and choosing to ignore something improper.

clue.text: Account for sudden noise

definitions.meaning: a written or spoken description of events
a loud bang, such as a gunshot

explanation.definitionFit: A report is both a description of events and the bang of an explosion or gun.

clue.text: Strange critters put in confinement

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters of the next word are arranged oddly

explanation.surface: Weird creatures are locked up in a cage.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrict is to confine or limit someone's movement, as when locking them up.

clue.text: Called after pilot's first crash

indicators.note: after places the telephoning word behind the single letter
first means take just the opening letter of the word pilot

parts.note: rang means telephoned, or called

explanation.surface: A pilot's opening move after being phoned leads to a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: PRANG is RAF slang for a crash, and the surface is fittingly about a pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: Prang is British slang, originally RAF, for a crash or collision in a car or aircraft.

clue.text: Converted windmill, perhaps, in which engines are repaired

definitions.meaning: a round dwelling, as a converted mill tower might be
a circular railway shed for locomotives around a turntable

explanation.definitionFit: A round home fits a mill conversion, and the railway term is a circular locomotive shed.

clue.text: Timothy's origins in ordinary people

parts.note: timothy is a meadow grass, so timothy's is the grass's
roots are origins

explanation.surface: A man named Timothy traces his family back to humble people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Timothy' looks like a man's name but is timothy grass, a pasture plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The grassroots are the ordinary members of a movement or party, as opposed to the leaders.

clue.text: An odd plant

parts.note: an gives the indefinite article A
rum is old British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: A strange-looking plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The arum is a plant family including lords-and-ladies and the arum lily.

clue.text: Many of them suffered the death penalty on a ridiculous charge

definitions.text: Many of them suffered the death penalty on a ridiculous charge

parts.words: Many of them suffered the death penalty on a ridiculous charge
parts.note: reads as wrongfully executed prisoners, but describes the cavalry who died in the doomed charge at Balaclava in 1854

explanation.surface: Many convicts were executed on an absurd accusation.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'charge' is a cavalry charge in the Crimean War, not a criminal accusation, and the penalty was death in battle.
explanation.definitionFit: The cavalry brigade famously charged Russian guns in a blunder commemorated by Tennyson.

clue.text: Had been for makeover in advance

indicators.note: a makeover remodels something, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone had had a makeover ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something beforehand means doing it earlier, ahead of time.

clue.text: Antitoxins used in horseracing

indicators.note: used in signals the letters are found inside the word horseracing

explanation.surface: Drugs given to horses in racing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used in' points to letters inside hor-SERA-cing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sera, plural of serum, are blood fluids carrying antibodies used as antitoxins.

clue.text: Cutting out sound coming from back around '91

indicators.note: around means the reversed word encloses the Roman number
back tells us to read the word for sound backwards

parts.note: a noise is a sound
XCI is 91 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Removing a sound recorded in about 1991.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the sound word into ESION, which goes 'around' the Roman number; 'coming from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An excision is a surgical removal, the act of cutting something out.

clue.text: Such neat rhymes could be humbug

definitions.text: Such neat rhymes could be humbug

parts.words: Such neat rhymes could be humbug
parts.note: two words that both rhyme with neat, one a dessert word and the other food, together naming a confection such as a humbug

explanation.surface: Glib rhyming verse may be nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'humbug' seems to mean nonsense, but it is the striped mint sweet; its name is two words rhyming with 'neat'.
explanation.definitionFit: A humbug is a boiled mint, an example of an old-fashioned confection.

clue.text: Saint, extremely earnest and a stickler for discipline

parts.note: St Martin of Tours is a well-known saint

indicators.note: extremely means take the outermost letters of the word earnest

explanation.surface: A holy man, earnest to the extreme, is strict about rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes the first and last letters of 'earnest'.
explanation.definitionFit: A martinet is a strict disciplinarian, named after a severe French army drillmaster.

clue.text: Funny parrot — it featured in a: sketch, perhaps

indicators.note: funny suggests the letters are messed about

explanation.surface: Monty Python's dead parrot comedy sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny' rearranges PARROT to PORTRA; the surface recalls the Monty Python dead parrot sketch, but the 'sketch' is a drawing.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketch of a person, a quick drawing, is one kind of likeness or picture of them.

clue.text: Direction taken by Tom's schoolmate

definitions.meaning: Harry, Tom Brown's friend at Rugby in Tom Brown's Schooldays

explanation.definitionFit: It is a compass bearing, and the surname of Tom Brown's best friend in the Victorian novel.

clue.text: Silver spike producing damage to finger

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a nail is a metal spike

explanation.surface: A silver spike causes an injury to a finger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damage to finger' is the definition, a torn piece of skin by the nail.
explanation.definitionFit: An agnail is a hangnail, a torn strip of skin beside a fingernail.

clue.text: Record World Cup year

definitions.meaning: an old gramophone record played at that many revolutions per minute
Argentina hosted and won the football World Cup in that year

explanation.definitionFit: Old shellac records played at that speed in rpm, and the 1978 football World Cup was in Argentina.

clue.text: Standard, or two better than that

definitions.meaning: a Roman legion's standard bore a bird of prey
standard is also golf's par, and two strokes under par has a bird's name

explanation.definitionFit: A Roman legion's emblem was the bird, and in golf the term means two strokes under par.

clue.text: Cutting a department in the police force

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of a British police force

explanation.surface: Budget cuts hitting one police department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' is not reducing budgets but sharp, as in a biting remark.
explanation.definitionFit: An acid remark is sharp and biting, synonymous with a cutting one.

clue.text: Field Marshal almost had foreign soldier retreating

indicators.note: almost tells us to drop the last letter of the word had

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

indicators.note: retreating means the soldier's letters run backwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier, foreign from a British view

explanation.surface: A field marshal nearly captured an enemy soldier who was falling back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts HAD to HA; 'retreating' turns GI to IG.
explanation.definitionFit: Douglas Haig commanded the British army on the Western Front in the First World War.

clue.text: Business organisation founded on intelligence

parts.note: suggests a spy network, but means a company that gathers and sells information, intelligence in the sense of information

explanation.surface: A firm built on spying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intelligence' suggests espionage or brains; here it simply means information.
explanation.definitionFit: A news agency such as Reuters is a business that collects reports and sells them to papers.

clue.text: A dance initially opening the season

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of the word dance

parts.note: a vent is an opening

explanation.surface: A dance begins the festive period.
explanation.definitionFit: Advent is the church season of the four weeks before Christmas.

clue.text: You'll report this deer, oddly, in late December

indicators.note: report means the word before is said aloud and we write what it sounds like

parts.note: You'll is pronounced like the word for the Christmas season

indicators.note: oddly means take the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of this deer

explanation.surface: A festive greeting: you will tell of a deer, strangely, in the Christmas period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'report' gives the sound of YOU'LL, spelt as the old word for Christmas; 'oddly' picks T, I, D, E.
explanation.definitionFit: Yuletide is the Christmas season, which falls at the end of December.
